session_start.title: [akmon] Role declaration
session_start.format_line: Before doing project work, state which role you are operating in, and restate it whenever you switch. Format: `🧭 role: <name> — <focus>`.
session_start.develop_line: - DEVELOP (build the project), agents and the roles they work in: {{agents}}
session_start.operate_line: - OPERATE (run/use from outside), agents and the roles they work in: {{agents}}
session_start.pick_by_operation: Pick the role (never an agent name) by operation: decompose an existing thing → review · construct a new structure/decision → architect · realize a decided structure in code → engineer. If unclear, ask.
session_start.pick_generic: Pick the role the task calls for, one of the roles listed above, never an agent name; if unclear, ask.
session_start.delegation_line: Delegation is the default for non-atomic work: before the first repository sweep, edit, or test run, decompose the task and delegate every independent sub-step to available subagents. Keep only decomposition, routing, synthesis, and owner dialogue in the orchestrator. Skip delegation only when the task is atomic or the harness exposes no subagents; state the reason. The work style sets the rest: delegating also hands whole athla and higher-tier calls to delegates; controlling leaves stages to sessions the developer starts and, where a reasoner, auditor or athlos implementer would be called, recommends which, for what and why. Controlling: a delegate's brief is in the developer's language.
session_start.memory_line: Also: read `{{root_name}}/memory/` at session start (project memory).

role_on_code_message:
[akmon] Role check — you are editing project code.
Editing code is **realization** → the `engineer` role. Discriminator: decompose an existing thing → `review` · construct a new structure/decision → `architect` · realize a decided structure in code → `engineer`. If you were assessing (`review`) or designing (`architect`) — or no role is declared — this is a switch: declare `🧭 role: engineer — <focus>` and follow its pipeline (code-flow + pre-commit: tests + lint mandatory before "done") before continuing. Restate the role on every switch (roles/README.md).
Design→code hand-off: before writing code, confirm the task is **landed in `{{tasks}}`** with a link to its design (design-flow step 8 Hand-off), and **re-read the backlog** to sequence it against other work (code-flow step 1 Take) — a cold engineer session must be able to pick this task from `{{tasks}}` alone.
analysis_before_mutation_message:
[akmon] Analysis-before-mutation check — you are editing a planning/design doc (backlog / design / ADR / requirements / akmon process).
Role: **assessing what is** (problems, state, conformance) is `review`; **constructing the design** (options, contracts, the chosen structure) is `architect`. Declare the role (`🧭 role: <name> — <focus>`) and restate it on a switch (roles/README.md).
If this turn is analysis-only — the owner asked you to analyze, explain, review, compare options, or identify what remains — STOP: report findings + a recommendation in chat and get explicit confirmation ("write it" / "record it" / "make the change") before editing. If the request was already an edit command, proceed. Rule: guardrails/_common.md § Analysis before mutation.
drift_score_text: a drift score of {{score}} (an edit or shell call counts 1, a read ½, the first {{grace}} calls of a stretch nothing)
delegation_roster: `k_explorer` · mechanical edits / doc-sync / test scaffolds → `k_mechanic` · gate loops → `k_validator` · code under a decided contract → `k_implementer` · load-bearing analysis → `k_reasoner`
delegation_nudge_message:
[akmon] Delegation check — {{drift_score}} since the last subagent delegation.
Delegation is the default: route by task kind (MODEL.md § Capability tiers; guardrails/_common.md § Route by task kind). Exploration/summaries → {{roster}}.
If this genuinely is orchestrator work (decompose / route / synthesize / owner dialogue), carry on — this reminder is advisory and fires once per drift episode (a subagent delegation re-arms it).
delegation_ask_message:
[akmon] Sustained delegation drift — {{drift_score}} with no subagent delegation. A read never carries this ask, so it lands on a call that changes something (guardrails/_common.md § Route by task kind).
Route the next steps to a `k_*` delegate — exploration/summaries → {{roster}} — or confirm this is genuinely one of the orchestrator's reserved four (decompose · route · synthesize · owner dialogue) to proceed.
Fires once per drift episode (a subagent delegation re-arms it).
privilege_escalation_reason: Privilege-escalation guardrail: 'sudo' is never run by the agent. If elevated access is genuinely required, ask the owner to run the command themselves.
git_commit_no_ai_trailer_reason: Commit guardrail: no AI 'Co-Authored-By' trailer — the committer is the human. Remove it and retry.
git_commit_push_tag_merge_reason: Commit guardrail: the owner owns publishing. push and tag are the owner's everywhere, a linked worktree's own branch included — confirm this is explicitly requested.
git_commit_history_reason: Commit guardrail: git {{subcommand}} writes history in {{where}}. The agent writes history only inside a linked worktree, on that worktree's own branch; anywhere else it is the owner's — confirm explicitly, or run it in a worktree.
git_commit_ref_reason: Commit guardrail: git {{subcommand}} moves, renames or deletes {{target}}. The agent moves, renames or deletes no ref but its own `_aitna/` job branches, and removes or moves no worktree, in any directory — confirm explicitly, or leave it to the owner.
git_commit_ref_target_stdin: the refs named on its standard input
browser_reason: Browser guardrail: the shared browser is the developer's session's tool, and this run may not drive it. Use the ordinary web request (WebFetch, WebSearch) instead.
browser_reason_delegated: Browser guardrail: the shared browser is the developer's session's tool, and a delegated agent does not drive it. Use the ordinary web request (WebFetch, WebSearch) instead; if the step needs the browser, hand it back to the main session.
browser_reason_autonomous: Browser guardrail (autonomous run): the shared browser is the developer's session's tool, and an autonomous run has no developer to share it with. Use the ordinary web request (WebFetch, WebSearch) instead.
browser_attached_close_reason: Browser guardrail (attach mode): the browser is attached, so it is the user's own Chrome; the agent never closes its window or its page. Leave it open, and ask the user to close it.
git_commit_guard_crash_reason: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): the access matrix could not be read, or the guard failed while evaluating this command, so an autonomous run is denied — nothing was run. The owner restores the setup (`akmon verify`); a developer run is let through in the same case.
git_commit_where_unresolved: a directory the guard cannot resolve from the command text
git_commit_history_reason_autonomous: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): git {{subcommand}} writes history in {{where}}. An autonomous run writes history only on its own run branch (the one `AKMON_RUN_BRANCH` names, else a branch under `agent/` that starts with a task id) or in a linked worktree, never on the default branch, on `develop` or a `release/*` branch, on another branch of a checkout, on a detached HEAD or in a place the guard cannot resolve.
git_push_own_branch_reason_autonomous: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): git {{subcommand}} of the run's own branch {{branch}} is held for confirmation.
git_push_own_branch_forced_reason_autono: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): a force push or a deletion of the run's own branch {{branch}} is held for the owner's confirmation — rewriting its own branch is an open decision (ADR 0031/D07).
git_push_default_branch_reason_autonomou: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): push of the default branch is denied — an autonomous run never pushes {{branch}}, force or not (the default branch and `develop` are protected); its work reaches the default branch through a pull request the owner merges.
git_push_other_branch_reason_autonomous: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): push of {{branch}} is denied — an autonomous run pushes only the branch it is on, named by an explicit refspec (push.default, remote.*.push and a `-c` override can redirect a push that names none), and only if that is its own run branch (the one `AKMON_RUN_BRANCH` names, else a branch under `agent/` that starts with a task id).
git_tag_reason_autonomous: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): git {{subcommand}} is outside the repertoire an autonomous run is granted — the owner tags.
gh_pr_create_reason: Commit guardrail: {{program}} {{subcommand}} publishes the agent's work as a pull request, and publishing is the owner's — confirm this is explicitly requested.
gh_pr_merge_reason: Commit guardrail: {{program}} {{subcommand}} lands a pull request in its target branch, and merging is the owner's — confirm this is explicitly requested.
gh_release_create_reason: Commit guardrail: {{program}} {{subcommand}} publishes a release, and publishing is the owner's — confirm this is explicitly requested.
gh_pr_create_other_base_reason: Commit guardrail: {{program}} {{subcommand}} targets {{base}}, which is not the default branch, and publishing is the owner's — confirm this is explicitly requested.
gh_pr_create_reason_autonomous: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): {{program}} {{subcommand}} is held for confirmation.
gh_pr_create_other_base_reason_autonomou: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): {{program}} {{subcommand}} targets {{base}} — an autonomous run opens a pull request (merge request) only into the default branch.
git_config_push_write_reason: Commit guardrail: git config {{key}} changes where a push goes.
git_config_push_write_reason_autonomous: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): git config {{key}} changes where a push goes (push.*, remote.*.push, remote.*.pushurl, branch.*.merge, branch.*.remote and the like) — an autonomous run leaves that configuration as it is.
gh_forge_write_other_reason: Commit guardrail: {{program}} {{subcommand}} writes to the forge outside a pull request, and publishing is the owner's — confirm this is explicitly requested.
gh_forge_write_other_reason_autonomous: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): {{program}} {{subcommand}} writes to the forge outside a pull request into the default branch, which is outside the repertoire an autonomous run is granted — confirm explicitly or leave it to the owner.
gh_publish_reason_autonomous: Commit guardrail (autonomous run): {{program}} {{subcommand}} merges or publishes, which is outside the repertoire an autonomous run is granted — confirm explicitly or leave it to the owner.
git_push_implicit_target: the branch git's configuration picks (no refspec names it)
git_config_edit_target: a configuration file opened in an editor

git_ref_unconditional.replace: the refs it writes under refs/replace/

escalated_ask_suffix: [escalated ask→deny: the run is unattended — permission_mode={{permission_mode}}, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED={{attended}} — so 'ask' cannot be trusted to reach the owner (ADR-0025/D06, C31) — re-run from an attended session if this was genuinely intended.]
stale_guardrail_notice: ⚠ akmon: the rules in {{root_name}}/.akmon/ are not the ones this session's akmon ships ({{names}}). Run `akmon sync`, then start a new session — the rules are @-imported once at session start, so this session keeps the stale copy.
